title: Guest Incident Checklist Form
subtitle: What the responder does in the first minutes: care offered, scene made safe, evidence preserved, and the right people called.
description: An original first-response checklist for a guest incident. It records the responder and time of arrival, the immediate care offered, the actions taken to make the scene safe, evidence and scene preservation before anything is cleaned or repaired, notifications made, the handover to the case owner, and what remains open.
use_case: Use at the scene in the first minutes after a guest is hurt, becomes unwell, or reports a loss, when the responder needs a sequence that does not depend on memory. The checklist closes when the scene is handed to the case owner with evidence preserved.

sections.title: Immediate care offered
sections.guidance: Offer help, record the response, and never assess an injury.

blocks.label: Care steps completed
items: Asked the guest whether they need medical attention
Offered to call emergency services and recorded the answer
Called emergency services where the guest asked or was unresponsive
Stayed with the guest until help arrived or they declined further help
Summoned a trained first-aid responder where the venue has one on duty
Offered a private place to sit and someone to stay with them
Asked whether they want a companion or group contact informed
Recorded the time of every step rather than reconstructing it later
blocks.guidance: Responders offer help and summon trained assistance. They do not diagnose, treat, move an injured guest, or give medical advice.

fields.label: Care outcome
options: Guest left to seek own care

blocks.label: Care boundary for responders
blocks.guidance: This checklist records what was offered and what the guest chose. It is not a medical assessment, a triage decision, or a treatment record, and nothing in it should be read as advice about a person's condition. When in doubt, call emergency services and record that you did.

sections.title: Making the scene safe
sections.guidance: Protect the next guest before restoring the space.

blocks.label: Scene safety steps
items: Hazard area cordoned, barriered, or attended until controlled
Wet floor or spill signage placed and left in position
Equipment switched off, tagged, and taken out of service
Route diverted or an alternative route signed for guests
Broken glass or sharps cleared using the proper equipment
Affected room or space taken out of service in the system
Similar nearby locations checked for the same condition
Manager on duty attended the scene

sections.title: Evidence and scene preservation
sections.guidance: Most evidence is lost in the first hour by cleaning up.

blocks.label: Preservation steps
items: Scene photographed before anything was cleaned, moved, or repaired
Condition that caused the incident photographed close up and in context
Camera footage retention requested before the overwrite window
Footwear, clothing, or equipment described rather than removed
Any item retained was bagged, labeled, and logged
Witnesses identified and asked to give their details
Relevant logs, work orders, and inspection records identified
Cleaning or repair deferred until photographs were taken
blocks.guidance: Preserve and describe. Do not test, dismantle, or repair the condition before it is recorded.

sections.title: Notifications and escalation
sections.guidance: The right people, in the right order, with times recorded.

blocks.label: Escalation triggers
items: Emergency services attended or the guest was transported
The guest reported a head, neck, or back injury
An allergic reaction was reported
More than one guest was affected
The condition could affect other guests before it is fixed
The guest or a companion recorded video or asked for a written statement
A police or regulatory attendance occurred
The guest alleges venue fault
blocks.guidance: Any ticked trigger requires the responsible manager to be involved before the responder goes off shift.

sections.title: Handover and closeout
sections.guidance: Hand the scene and the facts to the case owner.

blocks.label: Handover confirmations
items: Times recorded for care, control, and notification steps
Photographs and footage requests confirmed as captured
Retained items logged with a holder and a reference
Witness details passed to the case owner
Interim controls described with a recheck owner and date
Incident report started while the facts are fresh
Record stored with restricted access under applicable privacy policy

blocks.label: What the responder observed, what remains open, and what the guest was told
